items.bold: ARAGHCHI LANDED ISLAMABAD — received by FM Dar + Field Marshal Munir. Witkoff + Kushner arriving Saturday.
items.text: France24 and Dawn confirmed: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi landed at Nur Khan airbase in Rawalpindi, Islamabad on Friday evening. AFP published the photograph. He was received by Deputy PM and FM Ishaq Dar, Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, and senior Pakistani officials. Dawn: "a small negotiating team accompanied the foreign minister. A second round of peace talks with the US was also expected and a logistics and security team from the US was already in the capital." WH Press Secretary Leavitt confirmed Friday: Witkoff and Kushner will leave for Pakistan Saturday morning. CNN: Vance NOT going — Ghalibaf not attending, so Vance staying in Washington but on standby. Vance's staff WILL be in Pakistan attending negotiations. This is the most significant diplomatic development since the Islamabad round one on April 12.

items.bold: Iran: "No meeting planned with US." Classic ambiguity — indirect Pakistan-mediated format likely.
items.text: Iran's FM Baghaei posted on X: "No meeting is planned to take place between Iran and the US. Iran's observations would be conveyed to Pakistan." IRNA: Araghchi's trip is for "bilateral consultations" with Pakistan. Tasnim: "Currently there are no negotiations with the Americans on the agenda." However — Araghchi IS physically in Islamabad. US envoys ARE arriving Saturday. Pakistani mediators will carry Iran's positions to the US team and vice versa. This is the indirect "proximity talks" format that has historically produced progress in Iran-US negotiations (similar to the 2015 JCPOA early framework). The public denial is a face-saving mechanism for Iran — they cannot be seen negotiating under military pressure. Araghchi's tour (Islamabad → Oman → Moscow) signals Russia and Oman are also being brought into the framework.

items.bold: BESSENT (AP): Iran will start shuttering oil production in 2-3 days. Kharg Island full. No waiver.
items.text: AP confirmed: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated the US does not plan to renew waivers for Iranian oil purchases. "Not the Iranians. We have the blockade, and there's no oil coming out. And we think in the next two, three days, they're going to have to start shuttering production, which will be very bad for their wells." Kharg Island — which handles ~90% of Iran's oil exports — is at storage capacity. When Iran shuts production wells, it is not simply turning off a tap — it causes long-term damage to well pressure and recovery rates. This is the most economically devastating pressure the US has applied since the blockade began April 13. Iran's $140M daily oil revenue is already zeroed. Well damage would compound the loss for years. This economic pressure may be what finally brought Araghchi to Islamabad.

items.bold: Netanyahu disclosed prostate cancer — kept secret 2 months during war. USS Rafael Peralta intercepts.
items.text: Al Jazeera confirmed: Israeli PM Netanyahu disclosed he underwent successful treatment for early-stage prostate cancer — a small tumour detected during routine check-up. "No residual disease." He had kept the diagnosis secret for 2 months, saying he did not want it released "at the height of the war" to prevent "false propaganda against Israel." Netanyahu is 76. His health disclosure during an active war and ceasefire negotiation adds uncertainty to Israel's decision-making chain. Separately: CENTCOM released an image of USS Rafael Peralta (DDG-115) intercepting an Iranian-flagged ship near Hormuz on Friday. The blockade continues to tighten. Pentagon: Secretary Hegseth at briefing railed against European allies, saying the Hormuz standoff "is much more their fight than ours" — signalling US frustration with European free-riding on US naval enforcement.

items.bold: WFP: Food prices in Gaza 85% higher. Acute food insecurity in 10 countries. Sudan fertiliser crisis.
items.text: CNN confirmed: WFP released a report Friday warning food prices in Gaza are 85% higher than before the Iran war. Acute food insecurity and malnutrition "alarmingly high and deeply entrenched" in 10 countries: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, DRC, Myanmar, Nigeria, Pakistan, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Yemen. Sudan imports more than half its fertilisers by sea from the Persian Gulf — WFP has had to divert food shipments through longer Red Sea route. This is the clearest quantification yet of the West Asia War's humanitarian impact beyond the conflict zone. For India: India's own kharif season (June-August) planting is at risk if Gulf fertiliser supply doesn't normalise. India imports ~30% of fertilisers via Hormuz corridor. The longer Hormuz stays closed, the deeper the food security risk for 1.4 billion Indians.

military.t: BESSENT (AP): Iran Will SHUTTER OIL PRODUCTION in 2-3 Days. No Waiver. Wells Permanently Damaged.

military.t: Araghchi → Oman → Moscow: Russia + Oman as Deal Guarantors. Most Serious Diplomatic Round Yet.
military.d: IRNA confirmed Araghchi's full tour: Islamabad → Muscat (Oman) → Moscow. This three-stop tour is structurally significant: (1) Islamabad = Pakistan mediating US-Iran proximity talks, (2) Oman = historic Iran-US back-channel (Oman hosted the secret 2012-2013 talks that led to the 2015 JCPOA), (3) Moscow = Russia as international guarantor, potentially the power that will guarantee Iran's security if nuclear concessions are made. Araghchi visiting all three in one trip signals Iran is building a comprehensive deal framework — not just trying to extend the ceasefire. The inclusion of Russia and Oman suggests Iran needs external guarantors before it can commit to any nuclear or Hormuz concessions. This is the most sophisticated and serious diplomatic architecture Iran has attempted since the war began February 28.

assessment.body:
Saturday 8:00 AM IST. The West Asia War's most important diplomatic day since April 12.

WHAT HAPPENED OVERNIGHT — THE SEQUENCE
• Araghchi landed Islamabad Friday evening — AFP photo confirmed
• Received by FM Dar + Field Marshal Munir at Nur Khan airbase
• Witkoff and Kushner confirmed departing Pakistan Saturday morning (WH Leavitt)
• Vance on standby — not going unless Ghalibaf attends, but his staff are in Pakistan
• Iran publicly says "No meeting planned with US" — but both sides are physically in the same city
• Pakistan will mediate proximity talks — Iran positions conveyed to Pakistan, Pakistan to US

THE ECONOMIC GUN AT IRAN'S HEAD
• Bessent (AP): Iran will shutter oil production in 2-3 days
• Kharg Island storage full — nowhere to put new oil
• Well shuttering causes permanent damage to pressure and recovery rates
• Iran's $140M daily revenue already zeroed by blockade
• Well damage compounds losses for years
• This is why Araghchi is in Islamabad — the economic reality is existential

THE DIPLOMATIC ARCHITECTURE
• Islamabad: Pakistan mediating US-Iran proximity talks
• Oman: historic Iran-US back-channel (hosted 2012-2013 talks → 2015 JCPOA)
• Moscow: Russia as international guarantor for Iran's security
• Qatar Emir called Trump — Gulf states pressing hard
• This three-stop tour signals a comprehensive deal framework — not just ceasefire extension

IRAN'S PUBLIC VS PRIVATE POSITION
• Public: "No meeting planned with US"
• Private: Araghchi physically in Islamabad, touring Oman and Moscow for guarantors
• This is classic Iran diplomacy — save face publicly while moving privately
• The IRGC's hardline position requires Iran to appear not to capitulate
• Proximity format allows Iran to engage without "surrendering to US pressure"

INDIA's MONDAY MORNING
• Markets closed today. Monday 9:15 AM IST = verdict
• Positive signal → Nifty 24,200-24,500, Brent $95-100, rupee recovery
• Stalemate → Nifty 23,600-23,800, Brent $105+
• Military incident → Nifty below 23,400, Brent $112-120
• Most likely scenario given Araghchi physically present and Bessent's well-shuttering warning: POSITIVE SIGNAL (probability upgraded to 50%)
• Petrol/diesel hike risk: reversed if Brent falls to $95-98

VERDICT: The West Asia War has reached its most consequential diplomatic moment since February 28. Araghchi is in Islamabad. Witkoff is en route. Iran's oil wells are 2-3 days from permanent damage. Pakistan, Qatar, Russia and Oman are all engaged as mediators and guarantors. The economic noose has tightened to the point where Iran's choice is simple: negotiate now, or watch its oil sector collapse permanently. India wakes up Monday morning to find out which choice Iran made.
